title: Basic English — Course 2, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 7

tasks.audioText: The engineering department will run a teamwork session on Thursday morning. Students will meet in Workshop 3 at nine fifteen. Each group should bring its project notes and agree on one person to record decisions. The tutor will explain how to divide tasks fairly and report progress. The session finishes at eleven thirty.

tasks.prompt: A group of students prepared a model airport lighting system for a college project. At first, two members wanted to do the same task, while nobody checked the materials list. The group made a simple plan, assigned responsibilities and held a short meeting every afternoon. They finished on time and presented the system confidently. Reading 1. What problem did the group have at first?
options: Nobody had prepared the presentation slides
The group had too little time to finish
Two members wanted the same task and the materials list was unchecked
The group had not agreed on a presentation topic

tasks.prompt: How did they improve their work?
options: They changed the project topic and worked separately
They made a plan, assigned roles and met regularly
They asked the tutor to complete the materials list
They asked the tutor to divide the work for them

tasks.prompt: Our team ___ the presentation when the tutor arrived.
Choose TWO ways to contribute to a team project.
options: Change the plan without telling anyone

tasks.prompt: A person who works with you in the same team is a ___.
A teammate has not understood the task. What should you say?
options: Let's go through the instructions together.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of team projects in a sensible order.
Write 60–80 words describing a successful team project. Explain your role, how tasks were shared and what the group achieved.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the project and the student's role are identified (0–2); the response explains how tasks were shared and what the group achieved (0–2); past-tense forms and the sequence of events are understandable (0–2); teamwork/project vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
